notes:
Saved jobs

Each schedule is its own job. “Blank / set assigned users” and “Move Chromebooks to their students’ schools” jobs each have a name, their own copy of the settings, their own org units (or all Chromebooks), and their own time and days. You can have as many of the same kind as you like, for example one per school.
Making one: set things up in Chromebook fleet → Assigned users as usual, pick the org units under “Which Chromebooks”, set the time and days, then click Save as a new scheduled job… and name it.
The tab stays free. Saving a job takes a copy of the settings, so you can keep using the tab normally without changing any saved job.
Your existing schedules carried over. The single morning schedules you set up before become saved jobs automatically the next time GAMbit starts.

The Schedules page
It lists every scheduled job: your saved jobs plus GAMbit’s own background tasks (roster sync, digest, automatic groups and so on).

+ New job ▾: make a job right there.
Edit… (or double-click): change any setting of a saved job.
Preview in Assigned users: inside Edit, this loads the job into the tab with a Save changes to the job bar. You can load the Chromebooks, preview what it would do, adjust it, and save it back.
Duplicate: copies a job, turned off. This is the quick way to make the same job for another school: duplicate, change the org units, turn it on.
Turn on / off: pauses a job without deleting it.
Change time & days…: works for GAMbit’s own background tasks too.
Run now, Open its page, Delete: run a job immediately here, jump to the page it belongs to, or remove it.

Jobs still run with GAMbit closed, as long as the PC is on and you’re signed in to Windows. If you switch PCs, saved jobs stay on the PC where they were made, since that’s where the Windows tasks live.
